sections.html: Parosphromenus sumatranus is one of the more commonly available licorice gouramis. It was described in 1955. IUCN Red List: Near Threatened. Maximum size 3.5 cm. TDS 0–50, pH 4.0–6.0, temperature 22–28°C.
Endemic to Sumatra, mainly the Jambi area.
Blackwater streams and swamps in Jambi and neighboring basins in Sumatra.
Keep a pair in 20 litres, or a group of 3 to 6 in 40 litres with caves and leaf litter.
Micropredator. They only eat live food, such as live baby brine shrimp, daphnia and blackworms.
Peaceful and very shy; give them plenty of hiding places.
Two body forms occur, one with a higher back and one leaner. Females have the same pattern as males with a fainter dorsal spot.

Cave spawner with a head-up courtship, sometimes in a tipped-over position. In a larger tank several pairs may court and spawn at the same time. The male guards the eggs and larvae until the fry swim free.

It was treated as a subspecies of Parosphromenus deissneri until 2005. It mixes the fin colors of the common licorice gouramis with the head-up courtship of the slim ornaticauda and parvulus group. Fins: light red bands in the dorsal and anal fins, and a round black spot at the rear of the dorsal-fin base. The caudal fin is plain pale red to black-red, sometimes with a very short filament. The pelvic filament is black. Coloration: brown body with a narrow dark band where the body meets the anal fin. Similar species: the black dorsal spot separates it from Parosphromenus bintan and P. deissneri, and its black pelvic filament separates it from bintan, which has a white one.
